compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Operational signals reach the tracker only through a human-launched sweep (ledger `tomophobic-stilllife-mayfly`), and the store's automated filers produced 24 bugs that were mostly serial duplicates (nine `[binding-drift]` in 14 days; eight `[heartbeat-canary]`, two for a deliberately paused bridge) because each auto-closed on green and re-filed on the next observation. The sweep's NOT-A-BUG bucket is dominated by patchset-scoped Verified Gate runs and superseded scheduled runs. Consumes the inbox layer [rebar:51ce-b03e-cff5-4e9c] and the notice type [rebar:ac3a-9ea7-530d-48f4] (`notice_suppress`).

## Approach

A portable operation `rebar alerts ingest --source cloudwatch|github-actions [--dry-run]` (library `rebar.ingest_alerts`, MCP `ingest_alerts`, write-gated) that polls with a watermark, normalises observations and files under `docs/bug-creation-contract.md` plus eight anti-noise rules. Any scheduler invokes it (the GitHub Actions cron is the next child): the portability answer.

- **Sources** behind one `AlertSource` protocol yielding `Observation{fingerprint, state, severity, title, detail, occurred_at, url}`; both shell out to the already-required `aws`/`gh` CLIs through an injectable `Runner` (the `scripts/canary_bridge.py` / `scripts/alert_dedup.py` seam) — no new dependency. CloudWatch: `aws cloudwatch describe-alarm-history` for alarms with prefix `alerts.cloudwatch.alarm_prefix` (default `rebar-`), fingerprint `cw:<alarm>`; alarm evaluation periods are the debounce. GitHub Actions: `gh run list` per allowlisted workflow file (`alerts.github.workflows`, seeded from the ledger: mirror Test Suite, Reconcile Bridge, Mirror Guard, Live External Integration, Terraform Drift, Verify Authorship Identity), events `schedule|workflow_dispatch|push` on `main`, conclusion `failure` only (never `cancelled`), fingerprint `gha:<workflow-file>:<first failing job>`. Never the patchset-scoped Gerrit Verified Gate; never `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` (its canaries own `heartbeat-alert`/`binding-drift-alert`).
- **Filing** (the contract): one open bug per fingerprint tag `alert:<sha1(fingerprint)[:12]>`, tags `ops-alert` + `untriaged`, `detected_by = alerts-ingest`, templated body, abort-if-empty.
- **Eight anti-noise rules**: (1) dedup survives close — the search covers open bugs and bugs closed within `alerts.regression_window_days` (14); a re-fire inside the window **reopens** that ticket (`rebar.reopen`, `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:455`) with an `ALERT_REGRESSED:` comment, outside it files a new bug linked `relates_to` the prior; (2) a `resolved` observation adds an `ALERT_RECOVERED:` comment, never closes; (3) flap damping — transitions of one fingerprint inside one run collapse to one observation with a count; (4) N≥2 for workflow failures — first sight is recorded as `pending` in the ledger, filed only when seen again in a later run (the `4527` precedent); (5) `suppress` — an active notice whose `notice_suppress` contains `ops-alert` or the fingerprint tag skips filing, counted as `suppressed`; (6) storm grouping — more than `alerts.storm_threshold` (5) new fingerprints in one run file **one** bug tagged `ops-alert-storm`; (7) caps — `alerts.max_new_per_run` (5) and `alerts.max_new_per_day` (10); exceeding either files one `ops-alert-breaker` bug and stops; (8) ≤1 marker comment per 24h per ticket (`alert_dedup.recent_marker_comment`).
- **Watermark + audit**: one comment per run on the ledger ticket (`alerts.ledger`, default the existing `ops-sweep` ticket) with header `INGEST <ISO> | window <start>..<end> | filed N reopened N repeated N recovered N suppressed N grouped N | pending fp…` — the convention `docs/user-guide.md` documents for `SWEEP`. The next run starts at that window end; a cold start uses 24h.
- **Writes** of one run go through `batch_write_and_push` (`src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:395`): one commit batch, one push, however many tickets it touched. `--dry-run` computes the full report with zero writes.
- **Priority**: P1 for alarms in `alerts.critical_alarms`, else P2 (alarm) / P3 (workflow).
- **Stale-claim notice** (producer added to `src/rebar/_commands/inbox.py`): for sessions subscribed to `ops-alert`, an `ops-alert` bug `in_progress` longer than `alerts.stale_claim_hours` (4) with no event by its holder yields one `stale_claim` item. Notification only — no release.
- **Run report** `alerts_ingest.schema.json` (counts + per-fingerprint dispositions).

Positive rationale: fingerprint-keyed idempotent polling with a stored watermark is what elastic-recheck, Treeherder, and the GitHub-Actions failure→issue bots converge on; it needs no inbound endpoint and reruns are safe; reopen-on-regression removes the serial-duplicate class in this store's history. Failure dispositions: a source CLI error is transient (reported, watermark unmoved, retried next run); a dedup-search error fails toward filing (the contract's rule); a ledger write error is fatal for the run (no watermark advance, exit 1).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/alerts/` (new: `ingest.py`, `sources_cloudwatch.py`, `sources_github.py`, `rules.py`, `ledger.py`); `src/rebar/_commands/inbox.py` (`stale_claim` producer).
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py`, `__init__.py`, `_mcp_writes.py`, `_mcp_models.py`, `schemas/alerts_ingest.schema.json`, `schemas/__init__.py`, `types.py` + `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json` (regen), `docs/output-schemas.md`.
- `src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/writes.py`, `_cli/_registry.py`; `docs/cli-reference.md`, `docs/mcp-reference.md`, `docs/config-reference.md` (regen); `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`, `_config_sections.py` (`alerts.*` keys, each carrying a `# mechanism-ok:` marker).
- `docs/bug-creation-contract.md` (filer row), `docs/user-guide.md` (INGEST header; sweep optional).
- Tests: `tests/unit/alerts/` (fixtures captured from real `aws`/`gh` JSON), `tests/interfaces/cli/test_alerts_ingest_cli.py`.

## Testing

- Unit (temp-tracker store, fake `Runner` fed captured fixtures): workflow failure first seen → `pending`, second run → one bug, third → one repeat comment, fourth within 24h → none; closed bug re-fired at day 13 → reopened with `ALERT_REGRESSED:`, at day 15 → new bug linked `relates_to`; five transitions in one window → one ticket, `count == 5`; eight new fingerprints → one storm ticket; caps → one breaker ticket, no further filing; active suppress notice → `suppressed == 1`, no ticket (contrast: expired notice → filed); `resolved` → recovered comment, status unchanged; a CloudWatch alarm files on first sight (contrast with workflow).
- Store-effect: one run touching four tickets → exactly one tickets-branch push (existing push-counting seam); `--dry-run` → zero events.
- CLI subprocess: `--output json` validates; source CLI failure → exit 1, no watermark comment.
- Inbox: a subscribed session gets `stale_claim` for a 5h-old claimed alert bug, none for 3h. Gate: `make test`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] One fingerprint yields at most one open `ops-alert` bug across any sequence of runs, and a re-fire within 14 days of close reopens that bug rather than filing another; verified by `tests/unit/alerts/test_rules.py`.
- [ ] With an active `notice_suppress: [ops-alert]` a run files nothing and reports `suppressed`; verified by `test_rules.py`'s suppress contrast pair.
- [ ] Flapping, storms, and cap breaches each produce exactly one ticket per run, and a recovery observation adds a comment without changing status; verified by `test_rules.py`.
- [ ] A run's writes land as one push and `--dry-run` writes nothing; verified by `tests/unit/alerts/test_ingest_store.py`.
- [ ] `rebar alerts ingest --output json` validates against `alerts_ingest.schema.json`; verified by the schema coverage test.
- [ ] [non-codebase] A `--dry-run` of both sources against the live account and repository completes; its report (counts, window, zero writes) is recorded as a comment on this ticket before the cron child codifies the run.
